title: Resilience Responsibility Canvas and Rollback Primer
author: Ravi Patel
content:
Purpose:

This page provides a compact, actionable canvas teams must complete for any platform service before major rollouts. It unifies ownership declarations, bounded-context mappings, mandatory dashboard artifacts, and a short, operator-focused rollback primer. The intent is to reduce ambiguity during incidents and accelerate safe remediation without prescribing a single tooling path.

Scope:
- Applies to services in eng-platform: control plane components, runtime subsystems, and cross-cutting platform helpers (prefetch, cache coordinator, allocator).
- Not for one-off developer experiments; those must use a disposable canary environment.

High-level checklist (fill before production change):
1) Service identity and impact
- Service id: e.g., allocator-cohort-manager
- Customer-visible symptoms when degraded: increased p95, 5xx, slow-start failures, token cost surge
- Blast radius estimate: single-region / single-tenant cohort / all-tenants

2) Clear ownership (must be named)
- Engineering owner (code + rollout): full name and team handle
- Platform oncall owner: rotation alias or person
- Capacity owner: team owning GPU/quota reservations
- Escalation contact (secondary): email or slack alias

3) Bounded contexts and rollback scope (map explicitly)
- Code-level rollback: revert git ref or model variant tag? (yes/no)
- Config-level rollback: feature-flag toggle, routing table change, or infra config? (specify)
- Data-level rollback: is there a schema or downstream state that would prevent simple revert? (yes/no)

4) Minimum observability surface (non-negotiable)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, requests/sec, error_rate_by_code (4xx/5xx), token/sec, cache_hit_ratio
- Traces: distributed traces with deploy_id, model_variant, tenant_id
- Synthetic probes: minute-level probe per-region and per-priority cohort (canary + user-facing)
- Log fields: request_id, deploy_id, model_version, routing_decision, error_context

Dashboard requirements (template to copy):
- Summary row: current SLOs and a 24h sparkline (p95, error_rate)
- Deploy & flags: active deploy id and feature flags with timestamps
- Traffic breakdown: tenants, regions, model variants
- Operator tools: one-click links to toggle feature-flag, start rollback job, and run prefetch script

Alerting expectations (naming and gating):
- Use pattern: platform.<service>.<signal>.<severity>
- Each alert must include: Pager policy, runbook link, diagnostic queries, and mitigation hints
- Example thresholds (adjust per-service):
  - platform.allocator.p95.p0 -> p95 > 200ms for 5m with > 10rps
  - platform.cache.hitratio.p1 -> avg(kv_cache_hit_ratio[10m]) < 0.70
  - platform.runtime.error_rate.p0 -> increase(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total[5m]) > 0.005

Canary gating minimum flow (automatable):
1. Deploy to canary cohort (1% or defined tenants) behind feature flag.
2. Run warmup job for cache and any prepopulation tasks.
3. Monitor two gating signals for 15 minutes: p95 within 20% of baseline AND error_rate <= 2x baseline.
4. If gating fails, automated rollback to previous variant and create incident ticket.

Rollback primer (operator quick guide):
- When to rollback (require two corroborating signals):
  1) P0 alert (user-facing latency or errors) AND trace evidence tying deploy_id to errors
  2) Unexpected cost surge (token/sec increase) without proportional traffic increase
  3) Downstream integration failures (schema or contract breaks)

Fast rollback steps (concise):
1. Confirm scope: identify deploy_id and affected tenants. Take a dashboard screenshot.
2. Open incident channel and tag oncall and engineering owner.
3. Execute safest revert: toggle feature flag or repoint traffic to previous deploy. Prefer config toggle over infra rebuild.
4. Validate: run synthetic probes for 5–10 minutes and watch SLOs for 30 minutes.
5. If rollback cannot be applied: throttle traffic, engage capacity owner, and escalate to secondary oncall.
6. Record artifact links in incident ticket (deploy id, trace ids, dashboard snapshot).

Compact runbook template (copy into alert action):
- Name: platform.<service>.fast-revert
- Intent: immediate revert for customer-impacting deploys
- Preconditions: operator has feature-flag write and deploy rollback permission
- Commands: (examples)
  - Rollback variant (flag): curl -X POST https://flags.internal/toggle -d '{"flag":"<flag>","value":false}'
  - Rollback deploy: deployctl rollback --service <svc> --to-ref <git-sha>
  - Prefetch warmup: infra/scripts/prefetch-warmup --service <svc> --region <r>

Post-rollback actions and retro triggers:
- Required: open a retrospective ticket when any rollback occurs or any single-day SLO burn > 20%
- Postmortem must include: timeline, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, verification plan, and sign-off from engineering owner

Operational ownership matrix (copy to team pages):
- Primary oncall: first responder, executes rollback, initial comms
- Engineering owner: code fixes, roll-forward plan, postmortem author
- Capacity/infra: investigate preemptions, reallocate quotas
- Product/CS: customer impact assessment and blocking communication

Roadmap guidance (how to include in planning):
- Any planned change that touches the runtime kernel, quantization, or model-routing must include: expected latency/cost delta, fallbacks, dashboard updates, and a filled canvas before merge to main.
- Track temporary mitigations (hotfixes) in the technical debt log; each hotfix needs a scheduled durable fix within two sprints.

Retrospective template (short):
- Title: <service> rollback <date>
- Summary: what happened, impact, time to recovery
- Hypothesis: probable root cause with evidence
- Actions: owner / due date / verification steps

Appendix A — Example diagnostic queries (PromQL-like):
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- error rate: increase(http_requests_total{job=~"<service>",code=~"5.."}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{job=~"<service>"}[5m])
- cache hit ratio: sum(kv_cache_hits[10m]) / sum(kv_cache_requests[10m])

Appendix B — Common immediate mitigations (short list):
- High latency + 5xx: rollback deploy -> increase burst pool -> enable degraded-mode routing
- Token cost spike: rollback heavy model -> throttle non-critical tenants -> enable low-cost routing
- Cache collapse: run prefetch, rebuild warmset, throttle cache-populators

Maintenance and governance:
- Document owner: Ravi Patel (platform resilience)
- Review cadence: every quarter or after any service-level rollback
- When to escalate doc-level changes to leadership: if the same service class triggers >2 rollbacks in a quarter or if mean time to recover increases across platform by >25%

How to adopt this canvas:
- Copy this page into your release ticket, complete the fields, attach intended deploy ids and feature-flag names.
- Link the completed canvas to your PR and to any alert rules created for the rollout.
- Use the runbook snippets as the first lines of your alert actions so responders can act without hunting for documentation.
